The 1-50 patient-volume group (healthcare workers who see 1-50 patients) is the only bin showing a statistically significant BCG-vs-placebo difference in COVID-19 severity (p<0.05) by chi-square analysis.

Under the approved design (subject-level ITT 2x2: worst COVID-19 AESEV per subject; severe = max AESEV>=3; AEPT=='COVID-19'; Pearson chi-square without Yates correction):
  • 1-50    (n=835): BCG 414 not-severe / 9 severe vs Placebo 410 / 2  →  χ²=4.3298, df=1, p=0.0375  → SIGNIFICANT
  • 51-100  (n=129): BCG 58 / 1 vs Placebo 70 / 0                       →  χ²=1.1957, df=1, p=0.2742  → not significant
  • >100    (n=36) : BCG 17 / 1 vs Placebo 17 / 1                       →  χ²=0.0000, df=1, p=1.0000  → not significant
Fisher's exact (supplement) for 1-50: p=0.0639.
Sensitivity (inclusive 4-code COVID AEPT set, same framing): no bin significant (1-50 p=0.0763).
